the most common questions that comes up
is about polarity and that's why can I
MIG weld on DC but I have to use AC when
I TIG weld aluminum. So, you use DC
electro positive, same as hard wire uh
on steel when you're MIG welding
aluminum. And that actually etches off
an oxide layer that sits on the aluminum
surface having the positive side of the
arc there. Now, the thing about an
electrical arc is most of the heat is
going to go to the positive side with
the electrons moving up in that

and that wire is entering the weld
puddle anyway, it goes into
the positive side, heats
up that wire, and that wire drops into
the puddle and takes the heat with it.

of the heat down into the material. And

most of the heat down here, it won't

surface. It's kind of like an M&M when

to switch to positive for a short period

layer off, then switch to negative for a
while to melt it and go back and forth.

positive here, that etches, puts the
